title: Moshoeshoe I
summary: Moshoeshoe I (born c. 1786, died 11 March 1870) founded the Basotho nation by uniting refugees of the Shaka-era upheavals. The Government of Lesotho says he moved his people to Thaba Bosiu in 1824. SAHO adds that he welcomed Paris Evangelical missionaries in 1833, won battles against British forces in 1851 and 1852, and asked for British protection after a defeat in 1868.

uncertainty.note: SAHO gives birth c.1786; the Government of Lesotho gives 1786. Both give death on 11 March 1870.

as_recorded.value: King Moshoeshoe I was born in 1786 at Menkhoaneng.
He migrated to Thaba-Bosiu in 1824 with his people.

where.modern_name: Thaba Bosiu, Maseru District, Lesotho (his stronghold and capital)
where.historical_name: Thaba Bosiu, capital of the Basotho (Sotho) kingdom, later Basutoland

importance.justification: The Government of Lesotho calls him the founder of the nation, and SAHO says he preserved his kingdom through the mfecane and colonial pressure.

sources.title: Botho, Diplomacy and Peace - Basotho Nation-building Cluster of Sites (Tentative List)
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: Start of his chiefship differs by source (SAHO says he succeeded his father in 1820; the Government of Lesotho says he became head of his clan in 1822), so the summary avoids it. Pin is the stronghold, not a birth or burial place: the Menkhoaneng birthplace is named by the Government of Lesotho but I have no coordinate page for it. UNESCO tentative-list entry gives Thaba Bosiu as S29 21 21 E27 40 14, about 100 m from the OSM way.
